title: AI for Service Management and Support

questions.question: What must AI support automation preserve?
options: The first-response time, even when the answer is still unverified
Service ownership, explicit escalation criteria, and support quality
The existing ticket categories, left unchanged by the new workflow
The agent headcount, so knowledge articles keep being written
questions.explanation: AI support should reduce friction without hiding accountability or service risk. Ownership and escalation criteria have to survive the automation.

questions.question: A service AI drafts good responses but corrected answers never feed back anywhere. What is missing?
options: The service scope - the workflow has not defined which ticket types it may handle
The confidence rule - uncertain drafts reach agents without being flagged first
The escalation path - there is no defined route for tickets the model cannot answer
The learning loop - corrections have to update the knowledge source for the next ticket
questions.explanation: The lesson closes its workflow with a learning loop and lists knowledge updates as one of its four controls. Without it, corrections never reach the knowledge source and the same gap reappears on the next ticket.

questions.question: What does the Python artifact produce?
options: A ranked support AI readiness plan with controls and rationale
A production ticketing system that routes incoming service requests
An automatic closure for tickets answered with high confidence
A service contract fixing the response times support commits to
questions.explanation: The artifact helps choose controls for support workflows before AI is introduced into them.

questions.question: Which control belongs to this lesson?
options: An SLA display that hides the breach risk so agents are not distracted
A knowledge base frozen at go-live so answers stay consistent over time
An escalation path that names where a ticket goes when the model is unsure
A service scope left open, so the assistant can attempt any incoming ticket
questions.explanation: Escalation paths preserve accountability. Service scope, a confidence threshold, and knowledge updates are the other controls this lesson teaches.

questions.question: When should service AI require stronger controls?
options: When ticket volume, SLA pressure, or escalation risk is running high
Only when tickets arrive in a language the support team cannot read
Only when the assistant drafts replies rather than classifying them
Only when the service desk runs outside normal business hours
questions.explanation: High-impact service workflows need stronger readiness controls. The signals are ticket volume, SLA pressure, knowledge gaps, and escalation risk.

questions.question: Why are confidence thresholds useful?
options: They let the assistant close low-risk tickets without any agent involvement
They prevent silent automation failure and trigger review or escalation
They rank knowledge articles so the most-used answer is suggested first
They set the SLA target that the automated responses are measured against
questions.explanation: Confidence thresholds keep uncertain cases in controlled paths and prevent silent automation failure.
